sample.card.btreeBody:
A balanced search tree with many children per node. Few disk reads, which is why most database indexes use it.

Well normalised tables ([[{nf}]]) usually need only a few of them.
sample.card.normalFormsBody:
**1NF:** atomic values only. **2NF:** no partial dependencies on the key. **3NF:** no transitive dependencies.

Once normalised, indexes make the queries fast, see [[{btree}]].

sample.welcome.body:
Everything here is made up and shows how Obtion works. When you are done: Settings › Remove examples.

### Capture
Press c or + and start typing. What has no place yet lands in the inbox.

### Sort in
The inbox holds an idea that mentions [[{relaunch}]]. "Sort in" suggests the project as its place.

### Places
An entry can live in several places: [[{relaunch}]] is under [[Work]] and with the client [[{customer}]].

### Pinning
This note and the areas below it are pinned: they stay at the top of the sidebar.

### Types and views
Project, task and card are types, and you can add your own – like [[{book}]]. Every type has a page with views such as table and board.

### Queries
[[{week}]] gathers what is due soon with a query block.

### MCP
Connect an MCP client in the workspace settings to read and change your entries through an agent.
